title: Wounds and Scars
subtitle: No one can make sense of why this war drags on.

trails.title: Discipline and Regulations
trails.description: Adherence to military regulations is mandatory for all soldiers, including arcanists.

content.text:
1. Respect all comrades equally, regardless of classification.

2. Execute orders exactly; no changes based on divination.

3. Do not neglect conventional science; bullets often outkill arcane powers.

4. You are fully accountable for entities you summon.

5. No mental surveillance, influence, or manipulation of personnel without authorization.

6. No arcane modification of issued equipment without authorization.

7. Conduct spirit contact only with another member present; limit to three minutes.

8. Know the alternative forms of your comrades.

9. Report and secure approval before using large rituals or high-level incantations.

10. Expect enemy arcanists and other supernatural threats during operations.

items.text: Wounds and Scars

items.speaker: Captain
items.text: Fix bayonets!

items.speaker: Captain
items.text: For Victory!

items.speaker: Captain
items.text: Charge!

items.speaker: Captain
items.text: Damn! Their cavalry's returned!

items.speaker: Captain
items.text: Hold the line! I'll shoot any coward that runs!

items.speaker: Captain
items.text: You, you're from the Arcane Support Company? Go get that monster!
She can't remember how she did it—perhaps her enemies were as exhausted as she was, or perhaps it was just the devil's luck.

items.speaker: Arcane Support Soldier
items.text: Ugh!
Struggling, fighting purely by instinct, she holds her heavily armored foe at bay.

items.speaker: Knight
items.text: *cough*
Time crawls to a standstill; her bayonet is stopped mere centimeters from her foe's throat by two armored fists.
Dost thou recall when once, in our youth, we fought over an apple tree?

items.speaker: Arcane Support Soldier
items.text: Let go of me!

items.speaker: Knight
items.text: No, damn it!
Thou wished to cut its wood and make us a fire to roast a chicken.

items.speaker: Knight
items.text: Umm ...
But I rebuked thee. For I believed the tree would bear fruit, and it would be the sweeter bounty of the two.

items.speaker: Arcane Support Soldier
items.text: *panting*
Thou didst find a bush with over-ripened berries and hurled them at me, crying that they should serve as my supper, while the chicken would be for thee alone. And I retaliated in kind.

items.speaker: Arcane Support Soldier
items.text: But ...!
Ere long, we were painted red with juice.

items.speaker: Knight
items.text: Ah!
"What a bloody melee we fight!" We laughed as we laid down our arms. What fun we had that day.

items.speaker: Arcane Support Soldier
items.text: No. I don't want to ...

But the battle thou fightest now shall not end in the gentle smears of red berries. What drives humanity to war? 
Could it be so different from what drove us to it beneath that apple tree?
I dare not imagine how a slaughter that has claimed the lives of millions could be waged for so small a cause.
That we should be brought to bloodshed, driven only by the fear of those whom we were taught to despise.
What immortal hand or eye could frame the cause behind these deadly ends?
Thou art more courageous than I, Marie. Never hast thou doubted thy conviction. So tell me, I pray ...
Is there some purpose in the war they now fight?
For I see no divine meaning to be found in this killing and dying.
Small-caliber rounds pose no real threat to her rocky exterior, but that does little to reduce the pain.
And healing comes slowly.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: Agnès?
No response. That was expected. But what she had not expected was the next voice.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Who's Agnès?

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: She ... Matters not. But what brings you here?

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: I'm taking you somewhere safe. Paravyan—that young man who came with me—is back at the village. He'll continue with our search.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Before you ask, I'm doing fine. Like you, I'm made of sterner stuff.
She rotates her arm, looking as if her wounds had all but disappeared.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: I checked over your wounds, but I have no earthly idea what to do with this gravel. I know how to treat flesh, not stone.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: But that wound won't be a problem for you, will it?

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: No. Ugh ...
Her physical pain is bearable. But the lingering echoes of her nightmare cause her to grit her teeth.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Were you dreaming? It seemed like a nightmare.
She locks her stare forward and away. There's field dressing for the wounds that truly pain her.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: I don't know if this will help.
She removes her gloves. It's a brisk and almost tender motion,
revealing deep slashing cuts across her palms.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: Could it be ... Are you ...

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: I am. But that battle is long over. You and I are no longer enemies.
The howls of their deadly melee still ring in her ears.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: It was a senseless fight. I hurt you.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: It wasn't your fault.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: In fact, I thank you for it. They thought I died fighting you—I used that as my opportunity to leave.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: For some time after that, I was with an international rescue team. We came under attack by the Manus for our efforts, but the Foundation intervened.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: Wait, then you remember me?
Marsha nods, a gentle, graceful motion, carrying the reassurance of a doctor at her patient's bedside.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: And you didn't. I was wearing a helmet. But you don't have a face one forgets.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: Marianne.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Hm?

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Oh, that's your name?

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Marianne. It's lovely.
She repeats it, stressing the syllables as if to remember it.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: Tell me, then, what do you know about Manus Vindictae?

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: They are a secret organization open to only pure-blooded arcanists. Simply put, their goal is to cause as much chaos as possible and eventually destroy all of human society.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: And this "Mother of Resurrection" is like a god to them?

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Something like that, yes. She died once, but they managed to resurrect her through some awful ritual.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: A resurrected madwoman?
Her disdain curdles into hatred. Fingers clench, like she's trying to crush something in midair.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: Then she is a false prophet, an imposter of the true resurrection.
Marsha seizes the opportunity to move to her side.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: The war between the Foundation and Manus Vindictae has lasted ages—longer, even, than this war.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: You and the Foundation share the same goals, and the intelligence you gathered may prove crucial for us.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: If you would be willing to share it, we may be able to reach a truce sooner. So, please mull it over.
Sentinel bows her head, giving her rifle a rough once-over.
She wipes away some of the blood and dirt that cakes the receiver, then one by one slots new rounds into its magazine.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: My search into Manus Vindictae began at the turn of 1918. Their documents, personal belongings, letters ... I sought and scrounged for every clue that might be found.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: From these, I learned of their mission to prolong this bloodshed, supplying both sides with arms of dreadful artifice. Then as now, I still do not understand why.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: I brought my evidence before the powers of my nation, but they cared not. So, I spoke out against them, still hoping they might awaken to this madness.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: But my words went unheeded. Worse, they turned against me, hiding even the very name of Manus Vindicate from all their publications and letters.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: There is no longer any truth in the words they print; only lies meant to stir the pride of youth to deadly, pointless slaughter ... youths who were but children when the war began.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: That is why I have turned to this—to killing the ones who incited this war. It was the only choice I had left.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: Perhaps it has all been for naught, but at least I have put deeds to words. What has the Foundation done?
The accusation forces her into a stammering defense.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: We have done more than you know. But I'm not authorized to tell you.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: You expect me to offer all I know to you, yet still withhold your trust.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: I'm sorry. No, I suppose that isn't fair of us. If there is anything we can offer in exchange to make a deal, I'll ...
But her efforts lose steam.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: I'll try my best to honor it. But I can't guarantee anything.
A cold breeze cuts the stillness between them.
Sentinel lets out a slow and labored breath.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: I will give nothing to the Foundation, neither freely nor for any bargain.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: But you, Marsha—you have my trust.
Marsha lights up at her patient's declaration.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: Follow me.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Oh. Of course!
